clue.text: One who puts up two placards?

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice stuck up in public, one kind of placard
a poster is a large printed notice, the second kind of placard

explanation.surface: A question about someone who hangs a pair of signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two placards' supplies both halves: one placard word, then another. The answer is someone who sticks up notices.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pastes notices onto walls and hoardings is said to put them up.

clue.text: Print which is left with no copper in it

indicators.note: the word in tells us the preceding pieces go inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture that has been left without any copper in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NO and CU (copper) inside IT, giving INOCUT, after L for left.

clue.text: Right of succession which is formal and there is nothing kind about it over the upper class

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
O looks like a zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for kind wraps the next pieces

parts.note: a genre is a kind or type

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: taken as written
U stands for upper class, as in the old U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: A stiff remark that inheritance by the eldest is formal and unkind to everyone beneath the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IT over U inside GENRE, giving GENITURE; 'over' works because this is a down clue. U for upper class comes from the 1950s U and non-U debate on British class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The right of the firstborn son to inherit the whole estate is the classic rule of succession.

clue.text: Sees term converted into a different period

explanation.surface: Someone sees one term of school changed into another length of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted into a different' rearranges SEES TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year academic term, a fixed period of teaching.

clue.text: Injection which turns people upside down inside

definitions.text: Injection which turns people upside down inside

parts.words: Injection which turns people upside down inside
parts.note: a medical injection of fluid that churns the insides; the clue also hints that people (men) appear upside down within the word

explanation.surface: A grim joke about a procedure that upsets the body's interior.
explanation.walkthrough: Old-style clue: MEN reversed (NEM) sits in the middle of the answer, but nothing in the clue supplies the outer letters, so it reads as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This procedure injects liquid into the rectum to flush out the bowels.

clue.text: Network in which a girl endlessly pursues me

explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SHE to SH, and 'pursues' places it after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is an open fabric of crossing threads, a net.

clue.text: Making a mistake about a piece of jewellery

clue.text: Make similar although no information exists in house

indicators.note: in tells us these pieces go inside the word for house

parts.note: a home is a house
O looks like zero, no
gen is British slang for information
is means exists

explanation.surface: Making things alike, even when no news is to be had at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O, GEN and IS inside HOME. GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: To homogenise is to make uniform throughout, so every part is alike.

clue.text: Plants which make a soldier go after sport

parts.note: sport in the sense of fun, amusement

explanation.surface: Greenery that sends a soldier off in pursuit of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go after' places GI behind FUN. Sport here means amusement, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms and moulds were long classed with the vegetable kingdom, hence plants in older usage.

clue.text: Loose morals met as a cause of destruction.

explanation.surface: Lax morality meets its ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like an adjective for the morals but it signals the rearrangement of MORALS MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent whirlpool, one that wrecks ships, is a destructive force.

clue.text: Democratic processes which make for closer battles

explanation.walkthrough: 'make for' rearranges CLOSER BATTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting in private, so no one sees the choice, is central to elections.

clue.text: Collection of notes, for example, found by a soldier in a river after the sun is up

in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

GI is an American soldier

explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a chord played one note at a time, a group of notes.
